problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-3,-2]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2xy-{y}^{2}+1 \\ x{y}^{2}-x+1\end{aligned}].
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting  at the point  $[-2,\,1]^{T}.$

| $[$ | $-2$ | $-6$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | {{field-1}} | $].$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} | $-1$ |  |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2xy-{y}^{2}+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2xy-{y}^{2}+1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-x+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-x+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x+2y & 2x-2y \\ {y}^{2}-1 & 2xy\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}2x+2y & 2x-2y \\ {y}^{2}-1 & 2xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2xy-{y}^{2}+1 \\ x{y}^{2}-x+1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}2x+2y & 2x-2y \\ {y}^{2}-1 & 2xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2xy-{y}^{2}+1 \\ x{y}^{2}-x+1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}2(-2)+2(1) & 2(-2)-2(1) \\ {1}^{2}-1 & 2(-2)(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}(-2)^{2}+2(-2)(1)-{1}^{2}+1 \\ (-2)(1)^{2}-(-2)+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & -6 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
